title: initiative-scoring-ledger-for-reliability-prioritization-and-rolling-allocations
creator: Sofia Ruiz
description:
Summary:
Design and deliver a reusable Initiative Scoring Ledger that automatically computes priority scores for Reliability initiatives across services based on normalized SLI targets, recent error-budget burn, customer exposure, and business criticality. The ledger will power: 1) a leaderboard in Console for PM/Eng prioritization, 2) rolling allocations of discretionary error-budget tranches, and 3) gating logic for canary rollouts and automated rollback policies.

Background and motivation:
We currently surface SLOs and error-budget burn in siloed dashboards, which makes cross-team prioritization manual and reactive. Teams repeatedly ask for clear guidance on whether to pause feature rollouts or shift resources into reliability work. A scoring ledger ties signals into a single, explainable score that can be used in roadmap decisions and runtime gating.

Goals (MVP):
- Ingest per-service SLI time series from Datadog/Prometheus and compute 7d and 30d burn-rate normalized to SLO thresholds.
- Calculate a composite Initiative Score = weighted function(SLO burn percentile, customer-impact tier, % of requests failing, recent oncall incidents).
- Expose ledger API (read-only) for Console and a webhook for downstream automation (canary gating, alerts).
- Provide an admin UI in Console to tune weights and view proposed rolling allocations (manual approve/apply).

Acceptance criteria:
- Composite score calculation documented (Confluence link) and validated against historical incidents (compare rank ordering to postmortem severity).
- Console leaderboard shows top 20 reliability initiatives with drilldowns to SLI trends and contributing factors.
- Automated allocation prototype: a workflow that proposes moving up to 15% of discretionary error-budget from low-risk services to high-burn services, requiring a two-step approval.
- End-to-end test: a canary rollout is automatically paused when the receiving service's Initiative Score exceeds threshold and error-budget shortfall persists for 12h.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We will use SLO percentiles (95th for latency SLIs) rather than mean to reduce masking of tail latency problems. This increases false positives for noisy traffic but better aligns with customer experience.
- Weighting: initial default weights = {slo_burn: 0.5, customer_impact: 0.25, incident_count: 0.15, request_failure_rate: 0.1}. We will surface these weights and allow org-level overrides.
- Normalization: to compare across services with different SLO windows and traffic volumes we normalize burn by service criticality and a volume-smoothing factor.
- Privacy: per-tenant telemetry will be aggregated to avoid exposing PII in the public leaderboard.

Telemetry and validation plan:
- Backfill 90 days of SLIs and run the scoring algorithm to validate that high scores correlate with postmortem severity.
- Hold a validation session with two SRE teams and two product leads to calibrate weights (scheduled 2026-03-18).

Integration points / artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Initiative+Scoring+Ledger (draft)
- Design mockups (Console): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-scoring-ledger-mocks
- Prototype PR (backend): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9824
- Datadog dashboard for verification: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/abcd-initiative-ledger-verify

Next steps:
1) Finish scoring algorithm doc and circulate for review (due 2026-03-05).
2) Backend prototype: ingestion and score compute (ENG sprint 2026-W10).
3) Console leaderboard UI prototype (DES review session 2026-03-10).
4) Validation and alpha with two teams (start 2026-03-22).

Notes:
- This ticket intentionally focuses on the tracking/decision layer; full automation of reallocations and billing adjustments will be a follow-up (tracked under PM-58012).
- We expect the initial rollout to be internal to reliability and platform teams before exposing to customers.
